runners_data.name: Tolebi
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has not won in recent runs and whose form figures of -04940 paint a bleak picture; Danny O'Leary claims 10lb but the horse has placed just once from eleven starts on similar going and needs a stronger pace than this race shape is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Tolebi has run over today's trip and going before, and fourth-place finishes two and four starts back show he's capable of mixing it with this field; drawn in stall five carrying 139 lb, the concern is a turnaround after finishing unplaced last time, just four days ago.

runners_data.name: Michael's Well
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with a win and a placed effort on Good ground, but returning after 86 days off and handled by a yard with a modest 14-day strike rate; being a true hold-up type, the congested rear of this small field means it is squeezed toward midfield and will struggle to find the clean passage its style demands.
runners_data.comment: Michael's Well landed a win three starts back and was second four starts back, so there's proven quality in the tank; he also has experience over today's trip and going. The risk is 86 days off the track — that layoff needs answering.

runners_data.name: Likedbymike
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning — five places from fifteen similar-going starts tell the story; racing fresh off a 12-day turnaround, this hold-up type will need the pace to be stronger than Bear On The Run is likely to set to reel in the leaders from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and a runner-up four starts back, Likedbymike arrives here fit on a 12-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going; winless in recent starts, she remains the one to beat on our top rating of 95.

runners_data.name: Port Arthur
runners_data.note: High-rated at OR 120 but reappearing after a 291-day absence with just two career starts on the board; W J Lee takes the ride and the horse has placed on both runs including a third on Good ground, though the near year off the track makes fitness the central question in any scenario where he wins.
runners_data.comment: Port Arthur returns from a 291-day absence winless in his last two starts, and ranked fifth of six on our figures, he makes this tough; has run over today's trip, and stall one is his sole tangible angle.

runners_data.name: Bear On The Run
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the field, returning after 353 days off the track with a win on Standard and a fifth on Good in his brief two-run career; Shane Foley's judgment of pace will be crucial — if he can lead without being pressured, the race is run entirely to his profile.
runners_data.comment: Long absence of 353 days is the obvious concern for Bear On The Run, and our rating ranks her last of six — hard to fancy on figures. She does arrive off a win last time out and has run over today's distance and going, so the profile isn't entirely bare.

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.note: The only horse in the field with a win on Good ground (1/5f/GOO), making three of its last six starts on this exact going combination; a prominent racer by style who has been freshened up on a 12-day break, and Gavin Ryan's experience at Naas makes this horse dangerous if it can sit just off Bear On The Run's shoulder.
runners_data.comment: Focaccia bounces back into contention on the strength of her win three starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, returning fit on just 12 days' rest — the concern is her back-to-back seventh and eighth most recently suggest she'll need to rediscover that form.

races.paceDynamic: Bear On The Run is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-horse field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Shane Foley can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this six furlongs on Good turf at Naas. Port Arthur and Focaccia will press forward to prominent positions just off the pace, meaning the early order should settle quickly without a destructive speed battle developing. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Michael's Well is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield because Tolebi and Likedbymike are also rearward types competing for the same limited back-end space, meaning Michael's Well is unlikely to get the clean, late run that suits it best. This race shape — an uncontested leader setting a fair but not punishing pace — strongly favours prominent racers who can track close to Bear On The Run and pounce in the final furlong, rather than hold-up horses who depend on a strong gallop to close down.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bear Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bear On The Run leads without pressure and Focaccia or Port Arthur track within a length or two throughout.
scenarios.body: Bear On The Run controls fractions from the front, and the horses positioned prominently just off the pace — Focaccia and Port Arthur — are perfectly placed to mount a challenge at the two-furlong pole with no ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Override Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Port Arthur or Focaccia push hard enough early to pressurise Bear On The Run and test its stamina.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace raises the tempo and leaves Bear On The Run vulnerable in the final furlong, handing an advantage to the prominent pair who can respond to a stronger gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Picks Up Scraps
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the leaders tie each other up, leaving a clear late run available.
scenarios.body: A fast-run race would open a gap for Likedbymike, who has placed repeatedly on Good turf at this trip, to finish strongly through beaten rivals; however this scenario depends on a pace dynamic that looks unlikely given Bear On The Run's uncontested position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Form Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses to a crawl and the race becomes a sprint-finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race scrambles all positional advantages, making OR and raw ability decisive — Port Arthur's high official rating of 120 could prove telling in a dash to the line, though his 291-day absence is a significant question.

watchPoints.text: Bear On The Run has been off the track for 353 days — watch whether Shane Foley settles him cleanly in front or whether race-rustiness causes him to over-race and burn out before the final furlong.

Michael's Well is a genuine hold-up horse squeezed into midfield by the field composition — watch whether Jamie Powell attempts to push further back to find clear air, which could cost vital ground in a field of only six.
Port Arthur's 291-day layoff means fitness is unknown; watch how he travels at the two-furlong pole — if W J Lee is pushing along before the straight, the absence has likely taken its toll.
Focaccia has won on Good ground at five furlongs but has a mixed record stepping to six — watch whether Gavin Ryan elects to sit closer to the pace than usual to compensate for the extra furlong.

With three hold-up horses (Tolebi, Likedbymike, Michael's Well) all competing for rear positions in a six-runner field, watch the first furlong for unexpected positional shuffling that could disrupt the pace picture entirely.

races.name: Matchbook Betting Exchange Handicap

runners_data.name: Amiata
runners_data.note: Won last time at 5f on Good and has a win over 6f Good in her recent history; Colin Keane takes over for the powerful G M Lyons yard who are striking at 2/17 in 14 days, and this true hold-up mare will need a clean split late — 61 days off is the only mild flag.
runners_data.comment: Amiata brings two wins in his last five starts — a winner last time out and a winner three starts back — over today's trip and going, making him a potent threat at 140 lb; the 61-day absence is the one question mark.

runners_data.name: Red Evolution
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 4-year-old who finished second over 5f Good recently and has sound course form; Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking is a significant positive, blinkers on, and the step to 6f here suits a horse who has won over this trip at Good ground before.
runners_data.comment: Red Evolution won four starts back and was second five starts back, giving him a solid recent foundation, and he arrives here fresh enough on 16 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going. The top-rated runner on 140 lb, he's the one to beat despite back-to-back disappointing efforts.

runners_data.name: Gavoo
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3-year-old who was second in a 6f Good race in his penultimate start and won at the trip on Standish; visits Naas over 6f with cheekpieces on and trainer David Marnane (1/12 in 14 days) will need him to find daylight in a compressed field — was beaten here last time out.
runners_data.comment: Gavoo arrives here fit on a 16-day turnaround, and his second two starts back hints at strong contention under 137 lb from stall four — though his fifth last time out will need reversing if he's to land the spoils.

runners_data.name: Moltophino
runners_data.note: Consistent course-and-distance runner on Good ground who has found his level placing without winning recently; tongue strap and cheekpieces applied, Chris Hayes rides, and this 5-year-old's flat recent form (9th, 7th, 9th, 20th) makes improvement essential rather than optional.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Moltophino nonetheless brings distance and going experience to the table, and at 137 lb from stall 11 he remains a serious threat with our rating putting him third of eleven — though his recent string of unplaced efforts is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Spodo Komodo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a recent 6f win who represents the most complete lead profile in this field; Ronan Whelan is a top booking for the John Feane yard (1/5 in 14 days) and Spodo Komodo is the most likely horse to actually secure and control the front end — the danger is its 7f wins suggest it stays rather than quickens.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and a winner three starts back, Spodo Komodo brings solid recent form to this, and he has experience of today's trip and going; however, that unplaced run two starts back and a rating of 78 suggest he'll need to find more against the stronger-rated rivals here.

runners_data.name: Smoke Them Out
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has run over a mix of trips without winning recently; the 7lb claimer Sadhbh Tormey rides and the horse's recent record away from its trip (several 7f runs) leaves questions about whether it truly belongs at the sharp end of a fast 6f — most likely to crack if the pace war develops.

runners_data.name: Leveraging
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is a significant concern in a truly run 6f when the early leaders stop; Robbie Colgan rides for Sheila Lavery and although there is a 6f Standish win in recent form, the Good-ground record (0W0P from 2 runs) and the fade flag make this horse one to oppose rather than follow.
runners_data.comment: Leveraging has won two starts back but has finished unplaced on his most recent outing, and a ranking of 11th of 11 on our figures makes him genuinely hard to fancy; he has run over today's trip and returns after just 16 days, but that is about the extent of the encouragement.

runners_data.name: Clonmacash
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner who has placed third twice over 6f Good in recent starts for Adrian McGuinness (2/24 in 14 days); Declan McDonogh is an experienced navigator of tactical races, visor applied, and a fast pace directly suits a horse that can track and outstay tiring leaders.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Clonmacash does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and was third two starts back, though a seventh last time out tempers expectations; 130 lb from stall eight makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: Two recent wins over 6f Good underline raw ability, but this is a natural rear-end hold-up operator whose true style is squeezed toward midfield in a field packed with front-runners — the style fit score of 0.93 flags that its chance is structurally compromised, and Siobhan Rutledge will need significant luck in running to deliver its best.
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in his last six starts, but ranked tenth of eleven on our figures and carrying 130 lb makes him hard to fancy, despite the experience over today's trip and distance and his recent back-to-back victories lending some hope from stall one.

runners_data.name: Flaming Rib
runners_data.note: Veteran 7-year-old hold-up horse with visor on who has been competing mainly at 7f lately and steps back to 6f; like Gotta Catch'em All, its natural closing position is displaced by the volume of pace in this field, and a horse without a recent win on Good ground facing a speed duel it cannot influence from the rear is hard to place with confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Flaming Rib does bring distance and going experience to the table, and 12 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, a return of two fourths and an eighth from stall seven off 128 lb makes a bold bid tough to envisage.

runners_data.name: Lohoobb
runners_data.note: Progressive 3-year-old prominent racer who has placed second twice over Good-ground 6f-7f assignments and holds a perfect 7/7 record in similar-going races; W J Lee rides for Grassick and the 41-day layoff is the only query — the profile of tracking the pace and staying on is exactly what this race shape rewards.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Lohoobb is hard to fancy, though he has experience over today's trip and going, and his two runner-up finishes in recent starts suggest he isn't without ability.

races.paceDynamic: Leveraging, Spodo Komodo, and Smoke Them Out are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a strong early gallop over this 6f at Naas on Good ground — there will be no lack of pace, and the early sectionals should be genuinely testing. With three horses committed to making the running, it is unlikely all three hold their natural lead positions; Spodo Komodo, who has the highest finishing position in recent form at this trip, looks best placed to secure a berth up front, while Smoke Them Out and Leveraging (who carries a fade-in-finish flag) risk being burned off in a speed duel. The field also contains more hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Gotta Catch'em All and Flaming Rib are genuine closers by nature but are displaced into midfield in this projected shape, meaning neither is likely to enjoy the clean, wide-open run their style demands. A strongly-run 6f on Good ground, where three horses fight over the early lead, sets the race up squarely for prominent racers who can track the hot pace from just off the leaders and produce a sustained late effort — pure hold-up horses dependent on a clear gap from the rear are structurally disadvantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners ignite a fierce gallop and burn each other out, a prominent racer travelling smoothly just behind them inherits the race.
scenarios.body: The early leaders tie into each other from the first stride, leaving Clonmacash, Red Evolution, or Lohoobb to glide through on the bridle in the final two furlongs without ever being fully extended. Good ground at Naas rewards the horse who travels into the pace rather than having to chase it, and the prominent runners here have the course form and fitness to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds Honest Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner — most plausibly Spodo Komodo — asserts early supremacy and the others cede, allowing a controlled but honest pace to develop.
scenarios.body: Spodo Komodo's recent win at 6f and sound course profile give it the tools to dominate without burning at maximum speed, making it dangerous if it can find a rhythm without being fully pressured. A controlled lead at Good-ground pace still suits prominent types tracking just off the front, but the front-runner itself becomes a genuine winning player rather than guaranteed victim.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Thread Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns so hot that a gap appears wide late and a hold-up horse can find a clean run from off the pace in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Amiata, who is a true closer with Good-ground course form and a live recent win, is the most natural beneficiary, ideally placed to pounce if the field spreads and a lane materialises. Gotta Catch'em All, despite its natural hold-up style being compressed toward midfield in this map, carries genuine ability on Good ground with two recent wins and could threaten if it avoids traffic — though its displaced position tempers confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the early scramble for position causes interference or checks, shuffling the tactical order and opening the race to an unexpected outcome.
scenarios.body: A three-way battle for the lead increases the probability of a messy mid-race passage where horses lose their footing in the shape; Gavoo, who has Good-ground course experience and won fresh over this trip, is the type that can slot into a gap opportunistically if the race falls apart tactically. Moltophino's recent form is discouraging but its familiarity with this course and trip gives it a minor each-way foothold in a truly chaotic outcome.

watchPoints.text: Spodo Komodo, Smoke Them Out, and Leveraging all want the front — watch the first two furlongs for a speed war that could inflict serious damage on all three and leave them empty in the final 150 yards.

Leveraging is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish even in ordinary circumstances; if it burns fuel fighting for the lead against two rivals of similar intent, punters should be prepared for it to capitulate well before the line.

Gotta Catch'em All and Flaming Rib are genuine hold-up horses mapped into midfield because there is no room at the rear — watch whether either can find a clear run in the straight or whether they spend the race trapped in a wall of rivals with nowhere to go.

Red Evolution's addition of blinkers and the booking of Dylan Browne McMonagle for a yard quiet in the last 14 days (0/8) suggests connections believe headgear will sharpen a horse that was disappointing last time — watch if it travels more smoothly than its recent form suggests.

Amiata has had 61 days off since her last run for the in-form G M Lyons yard; Colin Keane's positive booking for a trainer firing at 2/17 in two weeks suggests she is ready, but hold-up horses can need a run back to peak sharpness — watch how she travels early as a guide to her fitness.

runners_data.comment: Caffu Zafeen has run over today's trip and going, and a rating of 61 — ranking him second in this field of 15 — marks him as a live threat under 142 lb from stall 14; the concern is that he's been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Tawaazon
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type with one win and three places from 13 similar-going runs, and has shown ability at this distance (2nd over 5f Good most recently placed); Terry Casey's 7lb claim is a useful asset and 16 days between runs suggests freshness.
runners_data.comment: Tawaazon has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating puts him narrowly top of this field, but he's winless in his last six starts — the second-placed effort two starts back is the main hook, and at 140 lb from stall eight he needs to reproduce that level.

runners_data.name: Reinforce
runners_data.note: Genuine back-runner who fades in the finish — a combination of the finishing concern flag and a record showing 2 wins and 3 places from 15 Good-ground runs makes this a difficult proposition in a race with one honest but not strong front-runner; Robyn Donaghue-Leahy rides for a small yard with minimal recent winners.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Reinforce nonetheless brings distance and going experience to the table, and our rating of 58 ranks him third in a field of 15 — the risk is that his recent string of unplaced efforts makes the improvement needed look significant.

runners_data.name: Dandy Land
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and race-shaper, wearing visor; STYLE_FIT of 0.93 flags that today's prominent role may be a slight compromise from its best, but the absence of a pace rival means it gets to dictate — trainer W McCreery quiet at 0/11 over 14 days is a context note worth holding.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but has shown enough ability to finish second last time out and third two starts back; she has run over today's trip and going before, and at 135 lb from stall 3, a repeat of her recent placed efforts would make her competitive.

runners_data.name: Hot To Foxtrot
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with four places from 11 Good-ground starts and real ability at 5f on this surface; pushed into a midfield map position because the true rear is overcrowded, so Jack Cleary will need to find a better-than-natural berth — STYLE_FIT discount applies.
runners_data.comment: Consistent sort in the mix, Hot To Foxtrot has finished third twice in her last five starts and has run over today's trip and going before — the main concern is she remains winless in recent starts, and 135 lb from stall 12 may test her.

runners_data.name: Practical Move
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type whose best form has come at 5f on Good (4th most recent); James Dowling's yard is quiet but Julian Pietropaolo's claim is legitimate, and this horse's profile over the right trip and going gives it an outside interest if it can sit handy.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Practical Move nonetheless has experience over today's trip and going, and a fourth last time out suggests some residual form; however, 135 lb from stall 13 makes life harder for a filly rated just 56.

runners_data.name: Undefeatable
runners_data.note: One career win on Good over 6f and the blinkered hold-up profile is genuine, but the map places it in midfield rather than where it wants to be; Sam Coen's 2lb claim is minimal, and at OR 51 dropping from a 1-from-13-on-Good record, the percentages are modest.

runners_data.name: Another Nice'day
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up filly who fades in the finish — a double-concern tag combining redistribution and finishing weakness; won at 5f on Good (most recent placed run) but the combination of being out of natural position and flagged finishing fade makes this a low-probability runner.
runners_data.comment: Four unplaced efforts in his last five starts make Another Nice'day hard to fancy, and our rating has him well below the field — though he does have experience over today's trip and going, and his sole recent win at least shows he can find the line.

runners_data.name: Platino Bianco
runners_data.note: Prominent-style horse with a win at 5f on Good recently and five placed runs from 15 Good-ground attempts; wearing tongue-tie and visor, Jack Kearney rides for a small handler but this is arguably the most naturally-suited prominent type behind Dandy Land and warrants close attention.
runners_data.comment: Platino Bianco won three starts back but has finished fifth in each of her last two outings, and the burden of 131 lb from stall 10 will test her further; experience over today's trip and going at least gives her a foothold.

runners_data.name: Star Allure
runners_data.note: 92 days off the track is the defining concern; a hold-up type with no wins or places on similar going from three runs, and the redistribution into midfield means Adam Browne-Souza's 7lb claim will need to work overtime just to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Star Allure has been out of the weights for 92 days and has shown little encouragement recently — though she has run over today's trip and going before, and stall four is her draw.

runners_data.name: Step Back In Time
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent-race type with three wins and four places from 15 similar-going starts — the experience and front-end style suit the map, though recent form has been poor (0090 last four); Nicola Burns's 2lb claim adds little and the 33-day break needs to be worked through.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Step Back In Time does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 33 days between runs suggests she returns fresh; however, her recent form makes it hard to see her breaking that duck here.

runners_data.name: Steel Magnolia
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly from W McCreery's yard (same trainer as Dandy Land, 0/11 over 14 days); visor worn, and strong on pace (four consecutive top-four finishes at 5f), but the redistribution note means her natural trailing position is contested — the form is there if she gets a clean passage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 11th of 15 on our figures, Steel Magnolia faces a stiff ask here; a third three starts back offers the sole bright spot, and she does have experience over today's trip and going from stall two.

runners_data.name: Luminessa
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with no wins or places on similar going from two attempts; Conor Cusack's 7lb claim is the most generous in the race but the 52-day layoff, tongue-tie, blinkered headgear, and a map position that is not her natural home combine for a difficult profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and unplaced most recently, Luminessa does at least have experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 55 suggests she holds more ability than her official mark implies — 52 days off is the main fitness query.

runners_data.name: Jackandthefox
runners_data.note: Prominent-type veteran at seven years who has shown consistent placed form (two places from 15 Good-ground runs); Wesley Joyce is an experienced conditional and this is one of the few horses whose natural map position matches its actual running style, making it an uncomplicated handicap each-way interest.

Winless in his last five starts, Jackandthefox has struggled to threaten throughout recent outings — a fifth last time out typical of his current level — though he has run over today's distance and going before and a low draw may at least offer some positional help off 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Livingston Range
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type whose best recent form has been at 6f rather than 5f; placed four times from 15 Good-ground runs but the redistribution away from its true rear position and Shay Wallace's 7lb claim for a quiet yard (0/5 last 14 days) makes this a long-shot situation.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pair of fourths the best he can offer in recent form, Livingston Range arrives from draw 9 carrying 122 lb and, while he has run over today's trip and going, he rates a clear outsider at 14th of 15 on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Dandy Land is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner sprint and, with no genuine pace rival to contest the early lead, should carve out a measured, controlled tempo from the outside of a gate draw in a 5f flat-track conditions that encourage front-end dominance. Platino Bianco and Step Back In Time are the most likely prominent types to slot in behind Dandy Land, giving the race a settled single-file shape rather than a chaotic pace battle. With Good ground and a straightforward track profile, an uncontested leader is difficult to peg back from off the pace in 5f, and the race shape points clearly toward the near-leads — those tracking Dandy Land within two or three lengths — being best placed. The field holds materially more hold-up types than can find genuine rearward positions: Hot To Foxtrot, Undefeatable, Another Nice'day, Steel Magnolia, Luminessa, Star Allure and Livingston Range are all true closers pushed into midfield by the map because the genuine rear end is overcrowded, meaning late-running scenarios are contingent on horses racing out of character.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dandy Land Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Dandy Land is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and set a sustainable honest pace, prominent trackers take the spoils.
scenarios.body: Dandy Land dictates from the front without a pace war, ensuring a fair gallop that neither blows up the leader nor plays into deep closers; horses positioned two to four lengths off the pace with natural prominence profiles travel sweetly into the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Near-Leads Surge Past Tiring Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Dandy Land fades in the closing stages having set a genuinely honest pace, the horses travelling prominently just off the lead inherit the race.
scenarios.body: Platino Bianco or Step Back In Time, having tracked comfortably, find the extra gear in the final 100 yards that Dandy Land lacks; this shape rewards those who were patient enough to not lead but aggressive enough to be on the heels of the leader entering the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Sweep Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected — perhaps with Platino Bianco pushing Dandy Land — and the front end ties itself up, midfield horses finishing with a run can get into the argument.
scenarios.body: Practical Move and Tawaazon, who carry genuine form at this trip on Good ground, have the class to pick off a race where the lead group has set too strong a pace to sustain; however this scenario depends partially on redistributed hold-up horses finding a position that is not their natural home, capping its likelihood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and every prominent horse ties up in the last 50 yards, the genuine hold-up horses closing from off a strong pace could mop up.
scenarios.body: Hot To Foxtrot and Undefeatable are the most credentialled closers but both are mapped out of their true rear-running role, meaning they are unlikely to be in the ideal position to execute a clean late run; this remains the least likely outcome given that only one front-runner sets a modest rather than suicidal pace.

watchPoints.text: Platino Bianco's early positioning is the key race variable — if it presses Dandy Land for the lead rather than settling second, the front end could tie up and fundamentally alter which shape unfolds.

With seven horses genuinely mapped out of their natural hold-up role, watch for a messy early split where multiple riders fight for midfield slots — any crowding or checking at the break will disproportionately hurt the redistributed closers.

Dandy Land's trainer W McCreery has returned 0/11 over the past 14 days; if the horse is below peak form, it may not sustain the lead long enough to set up a clean prominent-runner race, opening the door for Scenario C.
Star Allure returns from 92 days off — watch its pre-race market move for any stable confidence signal, as the long absence is the biggest unknown in the field.

The cluster of 7lb apprentice claimers (Terry Casey, Adam Browne-Souza, Orla Tynan, Conor Cusack, Shay Wallace) riding hold-up horses mapped out of their natural position creates a tactical riddle — inexperienced riders on horses needing a specific run may compound the style-fit penalties.

runners_data.name: Altimara
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Ross O'Sullivan who handles Good ground (9/15 sim-going) but has been racing over 8f recently and drops back to 7f here; 33 days between runs is fine but the back of a 19-runner field is not where you want to be finishing from in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Altimara has run over today's trip and going, and a third five starts back offers a rare flicker of hope, but just one unplaced effort in her last five runs and a trainer without a winner in 22 recent attempts make confidence hard to summon for this winless mare.

runners_data.name: Lough Leane
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type (6yo) dropped significantly in trip from 10f to 7f, and while the one win in 15 good-ground efforts came over a mile-plus, Jessica O'Gorman's 7lb claim softens the weight; 42 days off and this trip looks short of ideal on current evidence.
runners_data.comment: Lough Leane showed his best when winning three starts back, and he returns with distance and going experience to draw on at 138 lb from stall 18; the six-week absence is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Chester Nimitz
runners_data.note: Won over 6f Good last time out (OR=67) and Gary Carroll takes the ride — a naturally held-up horse whose best form has come over shorter; 26 days since last run, the 7f may be the right stretch if he can find a prominent early position rather than his usual spot.
runners_data.comment: Chester Nimitz has run over today's trip and going before and, ranked top of the field on our rating, he looks a strong threat; the concern is an unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners a horse with outstanding good-going form (10/15), a recent 6f win and a 7f place both on Good; his natural hold-up style will be squeezed in this 19-runner field but McMonagle's positional intelligence makes him one of the most dangerous if a gap appears late.
runners_data.comment: Rappell arrives on the back of back-to-back placed efforts — a winner last time out and a second before that — giving him a clear upswing in form, though his record in his last six starts otherwise reads patchy, and 136 lb from stall 13 may not help his cause.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Pairc
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard (1W) and placed on Going to Soft — the true racing style here is hold-up, and in a field already saturated with hold-up horses, W J Lee will struggle to find the natural position; STYLE_FIT of 0.92 reflects the compromise, and recent form 190-07 is mixed.
runners_data.comment: Recent form has been poor — unplaced in two of her last four starts and seventh last time out — though a winner five starts back shows ability; has run over today's trip and going, but 135 lb and a midfield ranking leave her needing a significant bounce.

runners_data.name: Dynamic Force
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner with a 7yo's race-reading ability, 14/15 good-ground record, and back after just 9 days — Sadhbh Tormey (7lb claim) means he carries less weight than his OR suggests; if he leads uncontested at a comfortable tempo, his strong-finishing 7f profile (1st and 2nd at this trip on Good) is formidable.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but a single win in his last six starts hints at inconsistency, and carrying 134 lb from stall 3 is the challenge — our rating of 68 offers modest upside in a 19-runner field.

runners_data.name: Mo Anam Chara
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Mark Fahey, returning 77 days later, who won over 8f Good and placed over the same; dropping to 7f may be sharp, but Ronan Whelan's booking and the yard's 1/12 recent strike rate suggest confidence — only 1/6 on similar going so conditions remain a mild query.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out but hasn't run in 77 days, and that layoff is the key question mark; she has run over today's trip and going before, and the 133 lb burden from stall 14 adds to the test for a filly who has shown she can win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Darkdeserthighway
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran whose natural style is at the back; the 7/15 good-going record and blinkered headgear show he needs things to work out perfectly — currently mapped into midfield out of his preferred position, which suits him less than a truly strung-out field would.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Darkdeserthighway at least has experience of today's trip and going, and a rating of 70 suggests some ability — but a modest latest effort dampens confidence, and 132 lb is a stiff ask from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Profit Surge
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over on a horse who has been placed four times in 15 good-ground starts without winning — genuine closer who sits far back and needs fast splits to cut through, but has been placed over 7f on Good (2nd) and trainer 1/5 over 14 days shows some recent intent despite the redistribution concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Profit Surge at least shows consistency — third last time out, and a second two starts back — and she has run over today's trip and going before, though carrying 132 lb from stall six will ask plenty of a mare rated just 62 officially.

runners_data.name: Sherekiya
runners_data.note: D K Weld's lightly-raced three-year-old hasn't run in 301 days, a significant absence with only three career runs showing modest form (4-5-7); Chris Hayes is a reliable pilot but the unknown quantity here — style listed as Unknown — makes her hard to place in any scenario with confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and returning after 301 days off, Sherekiya has experience of today's trip and conditions but a flat recent profile — fourth last time out — gives her something to build on, even if the layoff remains the key question.

runners_data.name: Irish Rumour
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type (11/15 good-going starts) for Jennifer Anne Lynch who has placed four times on Good turf at this trip range — 23 days between runs is fine, but positioned out of her natural berth in this congested field and the trainer's 0/2 recent form doesn't inspire.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a fifth last time out and her most recent placed effort — a second — coming two starts prior, Irish Rumour faces a stiff task from stall 15 carrying 131 lb; experience over today's trip and going offers slim consolation.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from Adrian McGuinness (2/24 over 14 days) whose record of 1W3P on Good ground and recent drop from 8f to 7f could sharpen his finishing effort; Cillian Rowan (10lb claim) reduces the weight significantly and his stalking role just off Dynamic Force is a natural tactical fit for this shape.
runners_data.comment: Third in one of his last four starts shows he retains some ability, but a sixth last time out and inconsistent recent form are harder to ignore; has run over today's trip and going, and 19 days off looks a fair enough freshener, though a mark of 61 leaves little room for error.

runners_data.name: Volendam
runners_data.note: Three previous placings and one win on Good ground, with a 1W2P record on similar going — J M Sheridan's booking and prominent style make him a natural beneficiary of a Dynamic Force-led tempo; form of 310252 shows consistency and the trip appears well within range.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 15 of 19 on our figures, Volendam faces a stiff ask, and a win in her last six starts hardly inspires confidence; however, she has experience over today's trip and going, and a second on her latest outing suggests she's been running consistently.

runners_data.name: Bear Right
runners_data.note: Jessica Harrington's three-year-old (T14: 3/31) has placed three times over 7f Good recently and is a genuine hold-up type pushed towards midfield in this crowded field — Shane Foley's experience is the asset here, but the STYLE_FIT of 0.92 and OR=64 suggest he'll need a race that falls apart in front of him.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without being a winner, Bear Right has finished third three times in her last five completed starts — yet to score, she does at least bring distance and going experience to this, and at 128 lb from stall 11, our rating of 72 gives her a squeak.

runners_data.name: Zheleznaya Dama
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who fades in the finish — the ⚠ tag is important here as 7f on Good may simply expose that tendency, despite a 7/8 good-going record; Rory Cleary's experience helps, but a finish fade in a 19-runner race is a significant liability.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled-up effort two starts back casting real doubts, Zheleznaya Dama is hard to fancy from stall 9 carrying 126 lb — though she has run over today's trip and going before, and was second last time out.

runners_data.name: Frosted Sky
runners_data.note: Three-run juvenile with a fades-in-finish flag, a 0W0P record, and genuinely limited form (8-8-6 in three outings on 5-6f) — stepping up to 7f here from 50 days off for Daniel McLoughlin, mapped out of her natural rear position into midfield, and the evidence doesn't yet point to a winning chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, the most recent of which came 50 days ago, Frosted Sky heads into this rated 8 lb below her official mark on our figures and ranks 18th of 19 runners — though she has run over today's trip and going before, which is at least some grounding.

runners_data.name: Summer Snow
runners_data.note: Top weight (142lbs, OR=72) for Peter Lawlor, and despite 3W4P on Good over a career, recent form of 0-9050 tells a cautionary tale — dropping back to 7f could theoretically sharpen her up but the trainer's 0/0 recent record and weight burden make this a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Rated 77 and ranked second of 19, Summer Snow brings strong claims at this level, has experience over today's trip and going, and 38 days between runs suggests connections have had time to plot this carefully — the concern is she's been winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Suerte
runners_data.note: Sheila Lavery's four-year-old (0W0P, OR=56) returns from 77 days off with a modest form string of 769-70 and a natural hold-up style displaced into midfield — good-going record (6/10) is moderate and there's no strong case to make for this level of form in a competitive 19-runner handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 17th of 19 on our figures, Suerte arrives after 77 days off a sequence of unplaced efforts — she has run over today's trip and going before, but there is precious little in her recent form to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Miss Ivor
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for P O'Rourke returning from 61 days, OR=54, fades in the finish and has shown nothing beyond mid-pack finishes in five career starts — the redistribution into midfield compounds an already limited set of claims at this trip and in this company.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with three unplaced efforts among them, Miss Ivor heads into this off a 61-day break carrying 119 lb from stall 19, and our rating of 46 — lowest in the field — makes her very hard to fancy, despite having experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Dynamic Force is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival to push him along — he can stride to the front from the gates and control tempo entirely on his own terms over Naas's flat, fair 7f on Good ground. With Land Of The Giants and Volendam likely to track from prominent positions just behind, the race will settle into a rhythm with Dynamic Force dictating from the front, those two holding a stalking role, and a large congested group rounding into the straight. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Phoenix Pairc, Bear Right, Profit Surge, Darkdeserthighway, Irish Rumour and Frosted Sky are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield because that berth is already over-subscribed — only the sharpest of them will find any daylight in a 19-runner sprint to the line. Given one uncontested front-runner setting a sustainable, measured tempo on Good ground, this race shape most favours patient prominent racers who can position just off the pace in the slipstream of Dynamic Force and produce a controlled challenge in the final two furlongs — true deep closers will face a difficult task in traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dynamic Force Controls Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Dynamic Force reaches the front uncontested and sets a sustainable tempo with no rival willing or able to press him.
scenarios.body: Dynamic Force (OR=64, 14/15 good-ground starts, strong 7f form at this trip) dictates every yard and wins a war of attrition, with only those close to him in the early stages conserving enough energy to challenge; Land Of The Giants and Volendam, tracking in prominent roles, are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Land Of The Giants or Volendam time their challenge to perfection and wear down Dynamic Force inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A steady tempo set by Dynamic Force means the race lacks a significant injection of pace until the home turn, allowing prominent trackers to cruise into the straight full of running; both Land Of The Giants (1W3P on this going band, 8f drop to 7f) and Volendam (1W2P good ground, Sheridan booking) have the class and position to pounce.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Picks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that the field concertinas entering the straight and a sharp hold-up horse threads through to score.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a runner like Rappell or Profit Surge to find a clear passage in a compact 19-runner field — Rappell in particular (1/6f GOO last time, 10/15 good-going record, Dylan Browne McMonagle) has the acceleration and the jockey to exploit a gap, while Profit Surge's consistency (0W4P but four seconds/thirds in this going band) keeps him involved; the redistribution of so many hold-up horses into midfield means traffic will be severe and this shape is genuinely harder to achieve.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Splits The Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large field (19 runners) causes severe crowding on the home turn and the race devolves into a scramble that rewards an unexpectedly positioned runner.
scenarios.body: With this many runners at 7f on a flat track, interference or a wide-draw nightmare could unsettle the pace scenario entirely and open the race to an unconsidered hold-up type catching a perfect split; Mo Anam Chara (returned 77 days ago, won 1/8f GOO, Ronan Whelan) and Sherekiya (D K Weld, unraced 301 days, big reputation) are the types who could benefit from a chaotic scenario where fresh legs and class override position.

watchPoints.text: Dynamic Force (Tormey, 7lb claim) sets off alone in front — if he hasn't been pressured by the 3f pole and is still travelling well, his course-and-distance winning form on Good ground makes him genuinely dangerous to oppose.

Land Of The Giants and Volendam are prominent types with strong Going records and apprentice/claim bookings — watch whether they can settle just off Dynamic Force's pace in the first 3f, because that position will be fiercely contested by a large field converging early.

With six genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield (Phoenix Pairc, Bear Right, Profit Surge, Darkdeserthighway, Irish Rumour, Frosted Sky), the home straight is likely to be severely congested on the stands side — horses that find clear air early in the straight will have a material advantage over those stuck behind a wall of runners.
Rappell (McMonagle) is the hold-up runner most likely to find a gap if the pace scenario creates any opening — his recent 6f win on Good and sharp finishing style mean he warrants monitoring

runners_data.name: Daler
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (1-2-3 in last three starts) over 10f on Good ground, trained by G M Lyons with Gary Carroll up; a hold-up performer who travels well through races and gets this 1m2½f trip, making him a natural beneficiary of any competitive pace.|
runners_data.comment: Daler arrives here in excellent nick — third last time out following a second and a winner three starts back — and has experience of both today's trip and going. The concern is whether he can defy a burden of 143 lb.

runners_data.name: Diamond Exchange
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here, Mrs John Harrington's 4yo has course-and-distance experience and Shane Foley knows how to manage a race from the front; five of his last seven starts have come at 10-12f and he won at 10f on Good — the key is whether he can hold on once challenged.|
runners_data.comment: Diamond Exchange won four starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, and with 20 days between runs she arrives fresh; the risk is that she's been out of the frame in three straight since that victory.

runners_data.name: Genoah
runners_data.note: D K Weld's yard is not active in the last 14 days, but Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride on this 5yo who has won at 12f on Standard and placed over 10f on Good; his natural hold-up style means he is unlikely to get the wide-open closing run he ideally needs, with his position on the map artificially forward of where he will want to race.|
runners_data.comment: Genoah ran a fine second two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 92 marking him out as a serious threat at 137 lb from stall 9; the risk is that fifth last time out shows he can disappoint.

runners_data.name: Nakasero
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's 5yo carries the tongue-tie and has finished second over 12f on Good-equivalent surfaces, but recent form includes finishes of 8th and 9th; the 7lb claimer Adam Grant is a notable factor, and this horse may lack the tactical sharpness for a well-controlled pace.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, though Nakasero did post a second four starts back to hint at better; the concern is three consecutive eighth-or-worse finishes since, and 137 lb is a stiff enough burden as he tries to reverse that slide.

runners_data.name: Pavilion End
runners_data.note: Charles O'Brien fields this 6yo who showed ability over 14f on Good (2nd) but has regressed sharply since — two 13ths in the last three starts; his genuine preference for coming from off a strong gallop is compromised by this controlled pace shape, where closers are not served.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Pavilion End does at least bring going experience to the table and shaped with promise when runner-up last time out, but a mark of 75 and stall one make this a tough ask for a horse who has struggled for consistency.

runners_data.name: Letiza
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this 6yo, a dual winner on Good ground at 10f, who is fresh off a second over 10f on Good last month; the going suits her, but she is a natural closer who will likely find the modest tempo set by Diamond Exchange insufficient to reel in those positioned closer to the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and a winner five starts back, Letiza has run over today's trip and going, but four of her last five have yielded just the one success, and her speed rating of 72 trails her official mark of 73 — stall 5 and 23 days fresh.

runners_data.name: Enchanted Lady
runners_data.note: A Olivier's 4yo has been placed at 12f on Good (4th) and this is likely a step up in distance class — 44 days since last run is worth noting; she falls into the hold-up bracket on her natural style and her limited form base (four runs only) makes her difficult to assess with confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 10 of 11 on our figures, Enchanted Lady faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 44 days off may have freshened her, but her recent form — seventh last time out — makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: My Girl Grace
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is a significant booking for G M Lyons' 3yo, who won on Soft over 10f and finished 7th over 12f on Good last time; at OR 80 she is the highest-rated runner by a slender margin and the premium jockey and trainer combination suggests she is expected to run well, even if her stable-companion Daler also competes.|
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back, but that seventh last time out is hard to ignore, and our figures rank her towards the foot of this field — she has run over today's trip and going, at least, offering some slim hope at 132 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Hamiyan
runners_data.note: D K Weld's 3yo has shown consistent placed form in softer conditions but the step up to 1m2½f on Good is an unknown — all five recent runs have been at 8f; headgear record (hg:p) suggests he is suited to prominent placement and Chris Hayes may choose to ride him closer than his natural style, making the redistribution note especially relevant.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Hamiyan does bring going experience and a fitness edge at 25 days since his last run, though fourth last time out and carrying 129 lb from stall 11 suggest he faces a stiff task to reverse recent fortunes.

runners_data.name: Big Dispute
runners_data.note: Kevin Thomas Coleman's 7yo has multiple wins and places over staying trips on Good ground including at 18-20f, but recent form figures of 6-9-10 suggest he is in a difficult patch; a true hold-up performer who needs a strongly run race over a longer trip than today — the distance and the controlled pace both count against him.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Big Dispute nevertheless heads this field on our ratings and has experience of today's trip and going; drawn in stall 10 carrying 126 lb, he looks the one to beat if he can recapture the form that rating suggests he's capable of.

runners_data.name: Covert Legend
runners_data.note: Maurice Ahern's 6yo has been remarkably consistent with four 4ths in his last five starts on Good and Standard, wearing a tongue-tie and visor; he stays 12f well enough but his flat trajectory of placed form without winning suggests he will run his race without threatening the principals in a steady-pace scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with four fourth-place finishes and a second three starts back his closest recent threat, Covert Legend ranks bottom on our figures here; experience over today's trip and going at least means conditions hold no surprises from stall 2.

races.paceDynamic: Diamond Exchange is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Shane Foley can control tempo from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over 1m2½f. The pace will be measured rather than searching, meaning the field will travel in a relatively compressed group through the middle stages before the race quickens in the straight. This shape — a lone leader setting a fair but unhurried pace — historically favours prominent racers who can travel just off the tempo and pounce, rather than deep closers who need a truly run race to get into contention. The field contains a significant concentration of hold-up horses (Genoah, Pavilion End, Letiza, Enchanted Lady, Hamiyan, Big Dispute, Covert Legend) who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they cannot all race from the rear in practice; of these, Genoah and Hamiyan — both with prominent headgear entries and tactical flexibility — are most likely to actually press forward and secure a position closer to Diamond Exchange than their natural style would suggest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Exchange is allowed to dictate an unchallenged, honest gallop and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Diamond Exchange, uncontested on the front end with Shane Foley in full control, sets a pace that is fair but not suicidal, and the stayers behind are left with too much ground to make up in the straight; horses who can travel prominently off the pace find themselves perfectly placed when the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to stretch the field and one or two horses who travel prominently off Diamond Exchange get a clear run into the straight.
scenarios.body: A horse like Daler or My Girl Grace, racing within striking distance throughout, produces a sustained run in the final two furlongs and picks off a tiring leader; this scenario suits those with proven Good-ground form at this distance who can quicken from a handy pitch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Exchange sets an unusually slow tempo that turns the race into a sprint finish from a tightly grouped field.
scenarios.body: With no genuine pressure from behind and a very modest early gallop, the race becomes a test of finishing speed rather than stamina, compressing the field and bringing short-priced hold-up types marginally more into play, though their redistributed map positions limit the benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than expected and several horses get the truly run race they need to close from the back of the field.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a genuine strong gallop that Diamond Exchange is unlikely to set alone, meaning it remains a low-probability outcome; horses tagged as redistributed hold-up types who end up racing closer than ideal are doubly disadvantaged if this shape fails to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Diamond Exchange (Shane Foley) — watch the opening two furlongs to see whether any horse attempts to press the leader; if Foley gets uncontested control the race shape is set and front-running chance increases markedly.

Genoah and Hamiyan — both natural hold-up types who may try to race closer than usual given the compressed field; if either forces their way to a prominent position early, the race becomes less predictable and more congested in the straight.

My Girl Grace (Colin Keane, G M Lyons) — the jockey-trainer combination warrants close monitoring; if Keane elects to track the pace rather than ride patiently, she becomes a significant threat to Diamond Exchange in the final furlong.

Daler running for the same yard (G M Lyons) as My Girl Grace — watch for any tactical split between the two Lyons runners that could benefit one at the expense of the other depending on how the pace develops.

The redistribution of seven hold-up types into midfield creates a congestion risk at the 3f pole; if the pace quickens suddenly, watch for any horse who gets a clean run on the outside versus those trapped on the rail.|

races.name: Irish EBF Ballyhane Stakes (Median Sires Series)

runners_data.name: South Dakota
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for A P O'Brien with three consecutive placed efforts, all at 7f-8f on good; dropping back to 6f here is a potential concern and Wayne Lordan will need the pace to be genuine to get his customary late run to tell.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in his last three starts, South Dakota has run over today's trip and going and brings solid placed form — third last time out — into this, with 134 lb from stall nine the main thing to overcome.

runners_data.name: Star Prospect
runners_data.note: Progressive Joseph O'Brien juvenile who won over 5f on soft and has placed twice on good; Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride and a step up to 6f looks likely to suit a horse who travels prominently and finishes well.|
runners_data.comment: Star Prospect is the top-rated runner in this field, with a win four starts back and thirds on two of his last four outings; he has experience of today's trip and going, and returns fit on a quick ten-day turnaround carrying 134 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Eighteenth Smiles
runners_data.note: Five career runs show consistent placed-to-midfield efforts; by nature a hold-up horse, though field congestion pushes her forward on the map — headgear (p) noted, and only four days since last run could leave her slightly short of peak freshness.|
runners_data.comment: Eighteenth Smiles has run over today's trip and going, and a third last time out offers encouragement, though he's winless in his last five starts and a return just four days later raises a fitness query — 130 lb from stall 3 is the added challenge.

runners_data.name: Ranting Duke
runners_data.note: Carries a lofty OR=120 with modest visible form (5-D-7) but did post a second at 6f on good going; the visor (v) is an interesting headgear addition and 30 days since last run means Ronan Whelan will need a clean break.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts — including a disqualification — and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Ranting Duke faces a stiff ask from stall 10 carrying 130 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Starlit
runners_data.note: Total unknown — no form, no going data, lightly-raced flag, but trained by Mrs John Harrington whose juveniles are often ready first time; Shane Foley steering is an encouraging sign and the flat Naas 6f could suit a well-bred newcomer.|
runners_data.comment: Starlit is unraced and completely unexposed, making her impossible to assess on form alone — but that very openness leaves plenty of room for improvement on debut, carrying 129 lb from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Alpe d'Huez
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed leader, with a 6f win already at Naas and solid form of 1-2-0; 47 days off the track is the key query, but Archie Watson's raiders often arrive fit after a break and Gary Carroll knows this course well.|
runners_data.comment: Alpe d'Huez has experience over today's trip and boasts a win three starts back, with a second two starts back franking that form — the main concern is whether 47 days off has left him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: El Domino
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery, who saddles as well as rides, which is a rare dynamic; one run behind him (6th over 6f good) and OR=120 reflects complete unknown status — lightly-raced flag warranted.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in recent starts, El Domino at least has experience over today's trip and conditions in his favour; the 18-day turnaround suggests he comes here fresh, though a sixth last time out and a mid-table rating leave him with plenty to prove from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Anglesea Bridge
runners_data.note: G M Lyons runner with two starts behind her, both at 6f on good, finishing 14th and 5th; modest visible evidence so far but the yard can improve juveniles sharply second or third time, and Robert Whearty keeps the ride.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Anglesea Bridge faces a stiff task here; that said, he has experience over today's trip and going, and 12 days since his last run suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Weekend Roar
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's colt has won and placed in his only two starts over 6f on good — the most course-and-distance relevant exposed form in the race outside Alpe d'Huez; 39 days off is manageable and W J Lee is an able partner.|
runners_data.comment: Weekend Roar won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but his our rating of 69 sits well below his official mark, and 39 days off the track leaves a fitness question to answer.

runners_data.name: Lily Bear
runners_data.note: Two starts over longer trips (7f-8f) with modest returns; 6f feels too sharp for a hold-up type bred to stretch out, and the OR=120 ceiling marks a horse whose ceiling is genuinely unknown rather than established.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last two starts and ranked eighth of twelve on our figures, Lily Bear faces a stiff task here; she does have experience over today's trip and going, and a run just 11 days ago keeps her fit, but that's slim consolation at these weights.

runners_data.name: Livenka
runners_data.note: The most progressive exposed runner on a 3-3-1 form string, with that win coming over 6f on good — this exact scenario; Colin Keane adds class in the saddle and G M Lyons' yard is in form (T14: 2/17), making her a legitimate prominent-style player.|
runners_data.comment: Livenka arrives on the back of a win last time out, and with experience of today's distance and going, she arrives primed to go close again — the main risk is whether her rating of 75 holds up against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Maeda Matsu
runners_data.note: Debutant trained by Ms Sheila Lavery with no public form; yard runs a modest strike rate but occasional unexposed juveniles outrun their marks first time, and Rory Cleary's booking at least signals confidence from connections.|
runners_data.comment: Maeda Matsu makes her racecourse debut from stall one carrying 121 lb — unraced and entirely unexposed, she is open to any amount of improvement and worth monitoring on first principles.

races.paceDynamic: Alpe d'Huez is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no other genuine leader to press her, she is likely to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 6f on good ground at Naas. Star Prospect, Weekend Roar, and Livenka will push forward to hold prominent positions just off the lead, creating a competitive early order but not a truly pressured pace — the tempo should be honest rather than scorching. Eighteenth Smiles is a natural hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains more prominent/hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, meaning genuine closers may find themselves racing closer than ideal. With a single uncontested pace-setter shaping a controlled, even gallop, prominent racers who can travel smoothly just behind Alpe d'Huez and produce a sustained late effort are best placed, making the P-style profile the primary beneficiary of this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alpe d'Huez controls and scores
scenarios.trigger: If Alpe d'Huez secures an uncontested lead and is allowed to dictate a comfortable tempo, softening the field for a long run to the line.
scenarios.body: Alpe d'Huez, proven at 6f at Naas and with a course win already banked, simply stretches clear at her own pace without a rival able to consistently match strides; Gary Carroll's patient front-running suits this horse ideally, and the good ground is no concern.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent pair collars leader
scenarios.trigger: If Star Prospect or Livenka travel smoothly in second or third and pounce on Alpe d'Huez inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Star Prospect has strengthened since a course win over 5f and now meets this trip for the first time, while Livenka's three-run form string of 3-3-1 shows progressive improvement and a 6f win; both are equipped to press Alpe d'Huez late if the front-runner ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse bursts late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and the race compresses, leaving a genuine closer a gap to exploit in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: South Dakota, trained by A P O'Brien and with consistent placed form, is a natural hold-up type and could benefit from a hot early sprint burning off rivals; Eighteenth Smiles, though redistributed forward on the map due to field congestion, retains genuine hold-up tendencies that could reward a late surge if the pace materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexposed debutant surprises
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly-raced unknowns — Starlit or Maeda Matsu — possesses untapped ability that the market and ratings cannot quantify.
scenarios.body: Debutants trained by quality yards such as Mrs John Harrington can arrive well-schooled and ready to hit the front on a flat, galloping 6f track; with OR=120 ceiling marks, either could outrun a weak market price if the handicapper and trainer have spotted something not yet seen publicly.

watchPoints.text: Alpe d'Huez — if she is allowed to stride clear unchallenged from the front, no rider moves early enough to close the gap before the furlong marker, and she wins from the front with her natural rhythm undisturbed.

Livenka and Star Prospect — both Joe O'Brien-trained prominent types will contest the same early ground, and if they bump or crowd each other leaving the stalls, both could be compromised for the run.

South Dakota — Wayne Lordan needs a genuine gallop to get his hold-up run to work over just 6f; if the pace is merely fair under Alpe d'Huez, South Dakota will have too much ground to make up in the final furlong.

Weekend Roar — Hugo Palmer's colt is the most straightforwardly course-and-distance-qualified runner bar Alpe d'Huez; watch the market move to see whether 39 days off has left him spot-on or just short.

Starlit and Maeda Matsu — both are debut runners with no public evidence; a significant move in their opening show prices before the off would signal stable confidence and should be treated as a meaningful late watch-point.

races.name: Hurling For Cancer On August 24th Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Dark Willow
runners_data.note: Six-year-old veteran with a weak finishing profile across her form (fades consistently) and 257 days off; her natural style is a deep hold-up but the crowded rear forces her into midfield on the map, diminishing her already limited chance.

runners_data.name: Zarenakarena
runners_data.note: Four-year-old debutante with zero form on record — entirely unknown quantity — jockey Jamie Powell and the Harty yard give little away; treat as a wildcard with no reliable pace profile.

runners_data.name: Zesty Belle
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type returning after 248 days off, with only two runs to her name both on Standard ground; the switch to Good turf is a genuine query and the layoff is significant.

runners_data.name: Acula
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien debut runner for whom no public form exists — the stable's 15/80 14-day strike rate signals volume and competitive intent; could hit the frame fresh if blessed with natural ability over this mile trip.

runners_data.name: Emiza
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's debutante, another completely unexposed filly on Good ground at a mile; Weld's 1/9 14-day record is steady rather than hot, but first-timers from this yard often need the run — though they can surprise.

runners_data.name: Estrallita
runners_data.note: Jack Davison-trained first-timer with no form to assess; trainer's 0/2 14-day record offers little encouragement and this is among the more speculative entries in the field.

runners_data.name: Mardi Gras Queen
runners_data.note: Stack-trained filly with a single run to her name — sixth over 7f on Healy — showing only early signs of ability; her natural hold-up profile means she's been pushed forward on the map, working against her chances in a steady-pace race.

runners_data.name: My Girl Jersie
runners_data.note: Three starts, three last-placed finishes on Heavy and Good ground, consistently fading late — her natural deeper role is compromised by redistribution to midfield, and the fade tendency makes her hard to support at any price.

runners_data.name: Nautic Star
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front runner; Shane Foley takes the ride for Jessica Harrington with a form string showing progressive placed efforts, and 16 days since her last run is ideal — she is the tactical pivot of the entire race.

runners_data.name: Never The Same
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes this ride for Joseph Patrick O'Brien — a powerful booking — and the filly's hold-up nature has been pushed into midfield by the crowded rear; front headgear worn, two runs showing modest form but the stable-jockey combo elevates her profile.

runners_data.name: Orellana
runners_data.note: H. Rogers debutante with Siobhan Rutledge aboard and no public form — one of several unexposed fillies making the race genuinely open; trip and going entirely uncharted.

runners_data.name: Shelton Spring
runners_data.note: Ran just six days ago and finished last of 12 over 7f on Good — a quick turnaround with a negative recent performance; her natural hold-up inclinations are squeezed into midfield on the map, and the fade flag compounds concerns.

runners_data.name: Sioux The Boss
runners_data.note: Finished last of 12 on Good ground on debut 66 days ago; wears a hood (headgear: p) and holds a natural hold-up profile that has been forced forward on the map — the combination of poor debut and unnatural mapped position makes her a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Sweetie Too
runners_data.note: Ran 10th of 10 on Good ground 63 days ago, showing a tendency to fade; a genuine hold-up type in a race where the late-running scenario is the least secure — needs a truly strong gallop that Nautic Star is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Terra Di Siena
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's filly ran 13th of 13 over 10f on Good 52 days ago — the step back to a mile may suit on paper but the form is weak; her fade tendency and deep hold-up style leave her needing more pace than this race will likely serve up.

runners_data.name: Venosa
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's filly ridden by Wayne Lordan brings the most extensive form profile in the field; her best effort is a third on Heavy ground and she has been tried across Good and Heavy — a natural hold-up type nudged into midfield by redistribution, but Lordan's placement and O'Brien's resources make her one to respect.

runners_data.name: Whatsin The Stars
runners_data.note: Ran 11th of 11 on Good ground just nine days ago wearing a hood; the rapid return is notable, the fade tendency is on record, and the deep hold-up profile combined with redistribution to midfield leaves her with a difficult task.

runners_data.name: Xirivella
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's mount for Noel Meade ran sixth on Good ground 30 days ago — front headgear worn, hold-up profile, Good-ground form is the one positive; Keane's booking adds market relevance and she is one of the more interesting unexposed runners in the hold-up group.

races.paceDynamic: Nautic Star is the sole confirmed front runner in this 18-runner fillies maiden over a mile at Naas on Good ground, and with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge her, she should be able to dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the front. The pace she sets is unlikely to be searingly fast — a lone leader in a large maiden field on Good turf tends to bowl along at a comfortable rhythm, which keeps the race together and can flatter those travelling well just off the pace. The field holds considerably more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions; Sioux The Boss, Shelton Spring, Never The Same, Mardi Gras Queen, My Girl Jersie, Dark Willow and Venosa are all genuine hold-up or prominent horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is oversubscribed — only Nautic Star is likely to actually secure a lead or near-lead berth without a battle. In a race where one horse controls the tempo unchallenged, the pace shape favours runners who can track closely just off the leader and produce a sustained finish — prominent trackers and mid-division closers with proven Good-ground form hold the tactical edge, while true hold-up types pushed into midfield out of role face a harder task if the gallop is steady.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nautic Star Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Nautic Star sets a comfortable, uncontested pace and the field settles into a processional rhythm behind her.
scenarios.body: She dictates throughout from a handy position, the race lacks a decisive injection of pace, and those tracking her closely within two lengths are best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutante Strikes On Debut
scenarios.trigger: If one of the several well-bred, lightly raced or unraced fillies debuts with natural ability that outclasses the exposed runners.
scenarios.body: A first-time-out filly from a powerful stable settles kindly in mid-division and produces an instant, unflustered finish on Good turf without the baggage of poor prior form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Late Finisher
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely unhurried and the field bunches, allowing a deep hold-up runner to scythe through on the rise to the line.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo compresses the field and sets up a sprint finish in the closing stages, which in theory benefits a true closer — but most hold-up types here are redistributed from their natural role, limiting the pool of genuine beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Nautic Star's control breaks down — through interference in a large field or a sudden pace injection from an unraced runner — and the race becomes messy.
scenarios.body: A scrappy, pressured pace scrambles positions and turns the race into a rough-and-tumble from which a more experienced or battle-hardened runner emerges.

watchPoints.text: Nautic Star (Shane Foley) must be monitored in the early stages — if she fails to jump cleanly or is crowded in an 18-runner field, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the race becomes unpredictable from the front.

Never The Same (Dylan Browne McMonagle / Joseph Patrick O'Brien) carries a high-profile booking that could generate significant market support despite modest form — watch the market move as it may signal stable confidence beyond what the form suggests.

Venosa (Wayne Lordan / A P O'Brien) is worth tracking in running; a natural hold-up type forced into midfield by redistribution, she has the most live form in the hold-up group and Lordan is expert at finding gaps in large fields.

The three O'Brien/Weld/Harrington debutantes — Acula, Emiza and Orellana — are unknown quantities that could dramatically reshape the race outcome if any of them debut with natural talent; watch opening show prices for last-minute market clues.

With so many runners carrying the fade warning and mapped out of their natural role, the race could easily string out into a one-two involving only Nautic Star and whichever close-tracking debut filly settles best — watch for any runner sitting second or third early and travelling smoothly.
